name: A null result for a non-nullable value type keeps the value on the frontend and sets the default on the backend
comment: A required number or boolean is a non-nullable value type in the C# model, which cannot hold null. Both sides warn. The backend sets the value the property has in a new object, such as 5 from a property initializer, and the frontend keeps its value until the save returns the default. A calculation that gives null again then changes nothing, so the two settle on the default after one save.
